doc.checkbox_a11y_keyboard: Toggle the checked state using the Space key.
doc.checkbox_a11y_label: Explicitly link label text with the input so it can be announced by screen readers.
doc.checkbox_anatomy_box: A custom visual part that represents the checked state.
doc.checkbox_anatomy_input: A hidden element that holds the actual checked state.
doc.checkbox_anatomy_label: A clickable text area that enhances affordance.
doc.checkbox_basic_usage_desc: Standard implementation of the Checkbox component. Use standalone or with CheckboxGroup for multiple selections.
doc.checkbox_choice_check_when: When multiple answers are possible, or for a single consent item.
doc.checkbox_choice_matrix_desc: Choose the most appropriate component based on the number and nature of choices.
doc.checkbox_choice_radio_when: When exactly one option must be selected from multiple choices.
doc.checkbox_choice_switch_when: When toggling a feature on or off results in an immediate change.
doc.checkbox_design_intent: Checkboxes are used to allow users to select multiple items from a list, or to toggle individual options (such as consent) on or off. The goal is to provide a clear indication of selection.
doc.checkbox_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the checkbox. Space toggles the checked state. Disabled checkboxes are skipped during keyboard navigation.
doc.checkbox_long_desc: Details and usage for the Checkbox component.
doc.checkbox_note_default: Generally, the default state should be unselected (off). This is crucial for user consent.
doc.checkbox_note_layout: Stack vertically and ensure a large tap area.
doc.checkbox_scenario_agreement: Terms of Service Consent: Placed as a required item before form submission.
doc.checkbox_scenario_filter: Search Filters: Selecting multiple categories to narrow down results.
doc.checkbox_scenario_newsletter: Notification Settings: Selecting multiple categories of information to receive in user profiles or settings.
doc.checkbox_state_indeterminate_desc: An intermediate state used when only some child elements are selected, such as in a 'Select All' checkbox.
doc.checkbox_when_to_use: Best for selecting multiple options or for Yes/No confirmations (e.g., terms of service consent).
doc.checkboxgroup_a11y_fieldset: Internally use <fieldset> and <legend> (or set appropriate WAI-ARIA attributes) to communicate to assistive technologies that these are a group of answers to a single question.
doc.checkboxgroup_anatomy_items: Individual options lined up within the group.
doc.checkboxgroup_anatomy_label: Explicitly states what the group is for selecting (e.g., 'Fields of Interest').
doc.checkboxgroup_best_practice_1: Always provide a group label (via Fieldset/legend or aria-labelledby) so screen readers can announce the purpose of the group.
doc.checkboxgroup_best_practice_2: Keep the option list short (≤8 items). For larger sets, prefer MultiSelect to avoid overwhelming the user.
doc.checkboxgroup_choice_group_when: When users select multiple options from a short visible list (≤8 items) and all options should be visible at once.
doc.checkboxgroup_choice_matrix_desc: Choose the right multi-selection component for the context.
doc.checkboxgroup_choice_multiselect_when: When the option list is long (>8 items) or space is constrained, and users benefit from search/filter functionality.
doc.checkboxgroup_design_intent: CheckboxGroup is a component for organizing related multiple checkboxes as a logical group and managing a common state (an array of values). It provides a consistent layout and operability in scenarios where users need to select multiple options at once.
doc.checkboxgroup_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus to the checkbox group. Space toggles individual checkboxes. Arrow keys move between options.
doc.checkboxgroup_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Checkbox Group component.
doc.checkboxgroup_scenario_filter: Search Filter: Specifying multiple product categories or brands.
doc.checkboxgroup_scenario_hobby: User Profile: Multiple selection of hobbies or special skills.
doc.checkboxgroup_title: Management component for grouping multiple checkboxes
doc.counterTextarea_a11y_spec: Use `aria-describedby` to link the textarea with the counter. Ensure the counter is announced by screen readers when the value changes.
doc.counterTextarea_anatomy_counter: A label showing the current character count and the maximum limit.
doc.counterTextarea_content_guidelines: Set a clear `maxLength` to make the counter more meaningful. The counter should turn red when the limit is exceeded.
doc.counterTextarea_design_intent: CounterTextarea helps users stay within character limits by providing immediate visual feedback on the current length of their input relative to the maximum allowed.
doc.counterTextarea_keyboard_desc: Follows standard textarea keyboard interaction. The counter updates as text is entered via keyboard.
doc.counterTextarea_long_desc: A wrapper for the Textarea component that adds a real-time character counter. Useful for fields with specific length requirements.
doc.counterTextarea_scenario_bio: User Bio: Restricting user descriptions to a specific character count (e.g., 160 characters).
doc.counterTextarea_scenario_comment: Comments: Providing feedback on the length of a feedback or support request.
doc.datagrid_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus between interactive elements. Arrow keys navigate cells. Enter activates cell actions. Escape cancels editing.
doc.dialog_best_practice_1: Use a Dialog only for critical interactions that require the user's full attention. For non-critical information, prefer Popover or Toast.
doc.dialog_best_practice_2: Always provide a clearly labeled close action (an X button or a 'Cancel' button) so users can dismiss the Dialog without completing the action.
doc.fielderror_basic_usage_desc: Standard implementation used to display validation error messages below input fields.
doc.fielderror_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. It is announced to screen readers via aria-live or aria-describedby.
doc.fielderror_long_desc: Details and usage for the Field Error component.
doc.fieldLabelContent_desc: Label text combined with required/optional badge
doc.fieldLabelContent_long_desc: FieldLabelContent renders the label text along with optional required or optional status badges.
doc.fieldLabelContent_summary: Component for displaying label text and required/optional badges
doc.fieldLabelContent_usage_desc: Used inside FieldTemplate to render the label area with required/optional indicators.
doc.fieldset_basic_usage_desc: Standard implementation for grouping related form elements with a legend.
doc.fieldset_disabled_desc: Disables all nested form elements at once using the disabled property.
doc.fieldset_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through the form elements contained within the fieldset in DOM order.
doc.fieldset_long_desc: Details and usage for the Fieldset component.
doc.fieldset_title: A container used to group related elements in a form, often with a legend.
doc.fieldset_with_legend_desc: Use the Fieldset.Legend subcomponent to provide a clear title for the group.
doc.fieldTemplate_a11y_desc: Automatically links the label to the input via htmlFor/id, and the error message via aria-describedby. The required/optional badge is hidden from screen readers.
doc.fieldTemplate_anatomy_content_desc: The slot where the actual input component (Input, Select, etc.) is placed.
doc.fieldTemplate_anatomy_error_desc: Displays a validation error message below the input when the field is in an error state.
doc.fieldTemplate_anatomy_label_desc: The text label displayed above (or beside) the input, linked via htmlFor.
doc.fieldTemplate_anatomy_required_desc: A small badge indicating whether the field is required or optional.
doc.fieldTemplate_best_practice_1: Always pass an id to the input child that matches the label's htmlFor to ensure correct accessibility association.
doc.fieldTemplate_best_practice_2: Use the direction='horizontal' prop for settings forms where space allows, but test responsiveness on narrow screens.
doc.fieldTemplate_choice_alt_when: When only a styled input shell is needed without a label — use InputBase instead.
doc.fieldTemplate_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether you need a full form field or only the input shell.
doc.fieldTemplate_choice_use_when: When the input needs a visible label, required/optional badge, and error message.
doc.fieldTemplate_content_guideline_1: Always provide a meaningful label text — do not rely on placeholder text alone.
doc.fieldTemplate_content_guideline_2: Keep error messages concise and actionable, describing what the user needs to fix.
doc.fieldTemplate_desc: Common layout (label, error) for form fields
doc.fieldTemplate_design_intent: FieldTemplate standardizes the layout of form fields by composing a label area, an input slot, and an error region into a single reusable wrapper, ensuring consistency across all forms in the application.
doc.fieldTemplate_i18n_desc: All labels and error messages should be passed as translated strings. The component also supports localized 'Required' and 'Optional' labels.
doc.fieldTemplate_keyboard_desc: This component itself doesn't have specific keyboard interactions, but it ensures that the nested input field is correctly associated with its label and error message for assistive technologies.
doc.fieldTemplate_long_desc: FieldTemplate provides the standard layout wrapper for form fields, combining the label, optional/required badge, input slot, and error message in a consistent structure.
doc.fieldTemplate_motion_desc: Error messages appear with a subtle fade-in transition to draw attention without being disruptive.
doc.fieldTemplate_scenario_1: Standard Forms: Wrapping every input in a signup form to ensure labels and errors are consistently placed.
doc.fieldTemplate_scenario_2: Table Inline Editing: Using horizontal layout for compact settings rows in a settings table.
doc.fieldTemplate_summary: Common layout for form fields (labels, error display)
doc.fieldTemplate_tokens_desc: Uses standard typography tokens for labels and error messages, and spacing tokens for consistent layout.
doc.fieldTemplate_usage_desc: Wraps any form input to provide consistent label positioning, error display, and accessibility association.
doc.indicatorSlider_desc: Sliding highlight indicator for Tabs, SegmentedControl, etc.
doc.indicatorSlider_long_desc: IndicatorSlider is an animated sliding highlight component that tracks an active element and smoothly moves to indicate the current selection.
doc.indicatorSlider_summary: Sliding indicator for Tabs, SegmentedControl, etc.
doc.indicatorSlider_usage_desc: Used internally by Tabs and SegmentedControl to display an animated active indicator.
doc.inlineEdit_a11y_desc: Ensure the component can be focused and activated via the keyboard. Use standard aria-labels for edit, save, and cancel actions.
doc.inlineEdit_best_practice_1: Do not use InlineEdit for long-form content; use Textarea instead for multi-line input.
doc.inlineEdit_best_practice_2: Ensure the edit state is obvious to the user through visual focus and icon changes.
doc.inlineEdit_choice_matrix_desc: Decide between InlineEdit and standard Input based on the editing context.
doc.inlineEdit_choice_use_when: When you want to seamlessly edit short text values in-place without opening a full form or dialog.
doc.inlineEdit_desc: A component that allows users to switch between a view-only mode and an editable mode in-place.
doc.inlineEdit_design_intent: InlineEdit provides a friction-less way to update information by removing the need for separate 'Edit' pages. It maintains context and reduces cognitive load during minor data updates.
doc.inlineEdit_keyboard_desc: Enter: Enters edit mode or saves the input. Escape: Cancels the edit without saving. Tab: Navigates through actions.
doc.inlineEdit_scenario_1_desc: Editing a username or a short bio directly on the profile page without navigation.
doc.inlineEdit_scenario_2_desc: Quickly renaming a task item or category in a list view.
doc.input_a11y_aria: When an error occurs, use aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby to explicitly link it with the error message.
doc.input_a11y_labels: Link a <label> to every input field and do not rely solely on placeholders.
doc.input_anatomy_container: Forms the border and background, clarifying the input area.
doc.input_anatomy_field: The <input> element where the user actually types text.
doc.input_anatomy_icons: Places for search icons, clear buttons, etc. (Prefix/Suffix).
doc.input_basic_desc: Standard implementation of the text input field for user data entry.
doc.input_best_practice_1: Keep the number of Input fields per form section to a minimum; group related fields and consider multi-step patterns for long forms.
doc.input_best_practice_2: Always pair an Input with a visible label — never rely solely on placeholder text as a substitute for a label.
doc.input_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on the amount and nature of the information to be entered.
doc.input_choice_number_when: Suitable for numeric-only input (including increment/decrement operations) such as quantities or amounts.
doc.input_choice_textarea_when: Suitable for long, multi-line text or comments.
doc.input_clearable_desc: Example displaying a button to clear input content.
doc.input_desc: Single-line input fields for text, numbers, or emails
doc.input_design_intent: Inputs (text fields) are the most basic components for obtaining short, free-form text information from users, such as names, addresses, and email addresses.
doc.input_ghost_desc: A simple style without a background color. It doesn’t emphasize the field normally, providing visual feedback only on hover or focus.
doc.input_ghost_i1: Empty: Placeholder suggests it is an input area
doc.input_ghost_i2: Hover: Displays a light background to notify it is intractable
doc.input_ghost_i3: Focus: Displays a primary-colored border to clearly show input state
doc.input_ghost_u1: Click-to-Edit UIs for titles on detail screens where display is primary
doc.input_ghost_u2: Noise reduction in screens with many input items like lists or tables
doc.input_ghost_u3: When you want to blend the search bar into the background
doc.input_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the field. Standard keyboard input is supported. Escape clears the field when clearable is enabled.
doc.input_long_desc: Details and usage for the Input component.
doc.input_outline_desc: Standard style with a border (same as default, but used when specifying explicitly).
doc.input_scenario_form: Contact Form: Entering various attribute information.
doc.input_scenario_search: Search Bar: Entering single keywords for site-wide search.
doc.input_title: A standard field for users to enter short text freely
doc.input_tokens_desc: Inherits tokens from InputBase (`--wim-color-surface`, `--wim-color-secondary` border, intent colors).
doc.input_variant_desc: You can change the style with the `variant` property.
doc.input_width_desc: By setting the `width` according to the length of the input content, you can visually convey to the user "what should be entered" (affordance). WIM UI provides semantic sizes (recommended) from `xs` to `xl`, which are responsive (automatically shrink to full width on smartphones).
doc.input_width_note: * Note that the `ch` unit is based on the width of the half-width digit "0", so when entering full-width characters (Japanese) or wide characters, the number of displayed characters may be fewer than expected. For multi-language support or general form design, the use of semantic sizes (`sm`, `md`, etc.) is recommended.
doc.input_width_usage: For detailed design guidelines, please also refer to the [Form UI Guide](/docs/guides-form-ui--docs#appropriate-width-setting-for-input-fields).
doc.inputBase_a11y_desc: Relies on the consuming component to provide aria-label, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid. InputBase itself is a visual container only.
doc.inputBase_anatomy_content_desc: The area where the actual input element or custom content is rendered.
doc.inputBase_anatomy_root_desc: The outermost wrapper providing border, background, and status styling.
doc.inputBase_best_practice_1: Never use InputBase directly in application code — use the higher-level components (Input, Select, etc.) instead.
doc.inputBase_best_practice_2: If you need custom content inside a standard-looking input, prefer InputBase over writing custom border/focus styles.
doc.inputBase_choice_alt_when: When the input needs a label, required/optional badge, and error message — use FieldTemplate instead.
doc.inputBase_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether you need a styled container only or a full form field with label and error.
doc.inputBase_choice_use_when: When you need only the visual shell (border, icons, states) without a label or error message.
doc.inputBase_content_guideline_1: Do not place labels or error messages inside InputBase — use FieldTemplate for that.
doc.inputBase_content_guideline_2: Limit right icons to 2-3 at most to avoid cluttering the input area.
doc.inputBase_desc: Shared shell wrapper for Input, Select, etc. (icons, clear button)
doc.inputBase_design_intent: InputBase serves as the structural shell for all text-input-like components. It enforces consistent icon placement, border treatment, and status styling (error, disabled) across Input, SearchInput, Select, and similar components.
doc.inputBase_i18n_desc: The clearAriaLabel and leftIconAriaLabel props should be translated strings for screen reader support.
doc.inputBase_keyboard_desc: Keyboard interactions are delegated to the child input element. InputBase itself has no keyboard behavior.
doc.inputBase_long_desc: InputBase is the shared shell wrapper for input components. It provides a consistent container with optional icons, status styles (error, disabled), and action buttons (clear).
doc.inputBase_motion_desc: State transitions (hover, focus, error) use CSS transitions for smooth visual feedback.
doc.inputBase_responsive_desc: Respects the width prop (xs–xl or custom value) and supports fullWidth for fluid layouts.
doc.inputBase_scenario_1: Wrapping a custom date picker trigger to get consistent border and icon treatment.
doc.inputBase_scenario_2: Building a tag input where custom content needs the standard input shell styling.
doc.inputBase_summary: Shared shell component for Input, Select, etc. (icons, clear button)
doc.inputBase_tokens_desc: Uses `--wim-color-surface`, `--wim-color-secondary` (border), and intent-based color tokens for consistent theming.
doc.inputBase_usage_desc: Used internally by Input, Select, Combobox, SearchInput and others to ensure a consistent visual and functional shell.
doc.inputgroup_basic_desc: Example adding a prefix to an Input using InputGroupText.
doc.inputgroup_fullwidth_desc: Using the fullWidth property expands it to the container width.
doc.inputgroup_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through each element in the group sequentially. Standard keyboard interaction applies to each individual input.
doc.inputgroup_long_desc: The InputGroup component is used to visually unify an Input with buttons or text (addons).
doc.inputgroup_multi_desc: Multiple InputGroupText components can be lined up.
doc.inputgroup_note: InputGroupText is for displaying information like units or prefixes. If clickable actions are needed, combine with the Button component.
doc.inputgroup_suffix_desc: Text addons can be added after the Input.
doc.inputgroup_with_button_desc: Action buttons can be placed next to the Input.
doc.label_desc: Descriptive text for input fields, including required/optional marks
doc.label_long_desc: A component for displaying descriptions or captions for form elements.
doc.label_req_opt_desc: Use the equired property for a required mark and showOptional for an optional mark.
doc.label_title: Descriptive text for input fields, including required/optional marks
doc.legend_long_desc: The Legend component is used to display a group title within a Fieldset.
doc.passwordinput_a11y_toggle: Explicitly state the state of the visibility toggle button (show/hide) using aria-label so that the current mode can be recognized by assistive technologies.
doc.passwordinput_anatomy_visibility: Visibility Toggle Button: Toggles between masking (●●●) the input content and displaying it as plain text.
doc.passwordinput_best_practice_1: Always default to the masked (hidden) state; never auto-reveal the password on mount.
doc.passwordinput_best_practice_2: Provide a confirmation field for new-password flows so users can verify their entry before submitting.
doc.passwordinput_choice_input_when: When the field value is not sensitive and masking is unnecessary.
doc.passwordinput_choice_matrix_desc: Use the right secure-entry component based on the sensitivity of the data.
doc.passwordinput_choice_password_when: When users need to enter sensitive credentials with visibility-toggle support.
doc.passwordinput_design_intent: PasswordInput is a component for securely entering sensitive information such as passwords. In addition to the function of masking the entered content, it provides a 'show/hide' toggle function so that users can confirm whether they have entered it correctly, reducing stress caused by entry errors.
doc.passwordinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the password field. Standard keyboard input is supported. Tab again reaches the visibility toggle button; Enter or Space shows or hides the password.
doc.passwordinput_long_desc: Enhanced input field specifically for secure password entry with visibility toggle.
doc.passwordinput_scenario_account: Account Settings: Confirming current passwords or setting new ones.
doc.passwordStrength_a11y_desc: Uses aria-live to announce strength changes and aria-valuenow to communicate the numeric score.
doc.passwordStrength_anatomy_label_desc: Textual representation of the current strength level (e.g., Weak, Strong).
doc.passwordStrength_anatomy_meter_desc: A multi-segment bar that changes color and length based on password strength.
doc.passwordStrength_best_practice_1: Show the meter near the password input field for immediate context.
doc.passwordStrength_best_practice_2: Use semantic colors (Red for weak, Green for strong) to aid quick understanding.
doc.passwordStrength_choice_matrix_desc: Use to guide users in creating secure passwords.
doc.passwordStrength_choice_passwordinput_wh: When only hidden input is required without visual feedback.
doc.passwordStrength_choice_passwordstrength: When password security is a priority for the application.
doc.passwordStrength_desc: Visual meter to indicate password security level
doc.passwordStrength_design_intent: To encourage users to create stronger passwords by providing immediate visual feedback during the registration or password change process.
doc.passwordStrength_keyboard_desc: As a purely visual indicator, it does not have its own keyboard focus but updates based on the linked input.
doc.passwordStrength_level_0_desc: Very vulnerable. Extremely short or simple.
doc.passwordStrength_level_1_desc: Vulnerable. Minimum length but easy to guess.
doc.passwordStrength_level_4_desc: Very strong. Highly secure with mixed characters.
doc.passwordStrength_long_desc: A visual meter that provides real-time feedback on the strength of a password based on predefined security levels.
doc.passwordStrength_scenario_1_desc: Helping new users choose a secure password during the signup flow.
doc.passwordStrength_test_desc: VRT covers color transitions for all 5 levels (0-4).
doc.passwordStrength_tokens_desc: Uses the semantic state colors: --wim-color-danger (weak), --wim-color-warning (fair), and --wim-color-success (strong).
doc.radio_a11y_group: Wrap in role="radiogroup" to tell assistive technologies that the choices are related.
doc.radio_a11y_keyboard: Move between items using arrow keys; selection changes automatically.
doc.radio_anatomy_button: The center dot indicating the selection state, mimicking traditional physical buttons.
doc.radio_anatomy_label: The item name. Selectable by clicking the text as well.
doc.radio_choice_matrix_desc: Decide based on the number of choices and whether the user needs to see all options.
doc.radio_choice_radio_when: When there are few choices (5 or fewer) and you want a bird's-eye view of all items.
doc.radio_choice_select_when: When there are many choices (6 or more) and you want to prioritize space saving.
doc.radio_design_intent: Radio buttons are used to force a single selection from multiple mutually exclusive choices.
doc.radio_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the radio button. Arrow keys move between options within the group, automatically selecting each option.
doc.radio_long_desc: Radio buttons allow users to select one option from a set.
doc.radio_note_default: It is recommended to set a default value for the most likely choice (e.g., Standard Shipping).
doc.radio_note_layout: Stack options vertically and ensure labels are clickable to improve usability.
doc.radio_scenario_payment: Payment Method Selection: Selecting one from credit card, bank transfer, etc.
doc.radio_scenario_plan: Plan Selection: Upgrading or downgrading a service plan.
doc.radio_title: A control that allows users to choose only one from a set of mutually exclusive options
doc.radio_when_to_use: Best for selecting exactly one option from 3 or more choices. Consider Switch for 2 states (On/Off) or Checkbox for multiple selections.
doc.radiogroup_a11y_group: Use role="radiogroup" and ensure standard behavior where items can be navigated between using keyboard arrow keys.
doc.radiogroup_anatomy_wrapper: A container that groups radio buttons. Can be arranged vertically or horizontally.
doc.radiogroup_best_practice_1: Always preselect a sensible default option; a required group with no default selection forces unnecessary cognitive effort.
doc.radiogroup_best_practice_2: List options in a logical order — most common first, or natural sequence (e.g., S → M → L → XL for sizes).
doc.radiogroup_choice_matrix_desc: Select the optimal component according to the number of choices and the importance of the operation.
doc.radiogroup_choice_radio_when: When there are about 3 to 5 choices and you want to keep all choices exposed at all times.
doc.radiogroup_choice_segmented_when: When you want to operate with a feeling closer to control buttons, such as switching ON/OFF or switching views.
doc.radiogroup_choice_select_when: When there are 5 or more choices and you want to save vertical space.
doc.radiogroup_design_intent: RadioGroup is a component for grouping multiple exclusive choices (only one can be selected) and managing a single selection state. It visually and structurally clarifies the constraint that the user must select exactly one.
doc.radiogroup_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the radio group. Arrow keys navigate and select between options within the group.
doc.radiogroup_long_desc: RadioGroup manages a set of Radio buttons.
doc.radiogroup_scenario_gender: Gender Selection: Single selection from limited choices.
doc.radiogroup_scenario_plan: Price Plan: Selecting one from Plan A, B, or C.
doc.radiogroup_title: Management component for grouping related radio buttons
doc.searchinput_a11y_desc: Uses role='searchbox' and aria-label. The clear button is keyboard-accessible. Supports live search results announced via aria-live.
doc.searchinput_a11y_label: Even with a visual icon, always set an accessibility label (aria-label="Search") to clearly state the purpose.
doc.searchinput_anatomy_clear: Displayed on the right when there is input, allowing content to be erased with one click.
doc.searchinput_anatomy_icon: Placed on the left, suggesting that the purpose of the field is 'search'.
doc.searchinput_best_practice_1: Include a visible search icon and placeholder text to clearly communicate the input's purpose.
doc.searchinput_best_practice_2: Provide a clear/reset button to allow users to quickly clear the search query.
doc.searchinput_choice_alt_when: When the input is part of a complex filter form (use Input with custom icons).
doc.searchinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the search interaction model needed.
doc.searchinput_choice_self_when: When you need a dedicated search field with clear button and search icon.
doc.searchinput_content_placeholder: Use an example of an actual search query (e.g., 'Quarterly report') as the placeholder, not instructions like 'Enter keyword'.
doc.searchinput_design_intent: SearchInput is an input component specialized for searching information. It comes standard with a search icon that communicates 'searching purpose' at a glance and a clear button to quickly discard complex search terms, optimizing the user's discovery experience.
doc.searchinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the search field. Standard keyboard input is supported. Enter submits the search. Escape clears the field when clearable is enabled.
doc.searchinput_long_desc: A component that provides a search interface.
doc.searchinput_scenario_global: Site-wide search placed in the header.
doc.searchinput_scenario_list: Search placed at the top of a table or list for item extraction.
doc.searchinput_title: A text input field specifically designed for search queries, including a search icon.
doc.select_a11y_1: Proper use of role="combobox" and role="listbox"
doc.select_a11y_2: State management for aria-expanded, aria-selected, and aria-disabled
doc.select_a11y_desc: The Select component complies with WAI-ARIA accessibility guidelines:
doc.select_a11y_listbox: Uses role='listbox' and indicates the currently selected item with aria-selected.
doc.select_a11y_scroll: Automatically scrolls so that the focused item is always within the display area during keyboard operation.
doc.select_adv_comb_desc: Search and grouping can be used simultaneously. Only groups containing options that match the search criteria will be displayed.
doc.select_adv_search_desc: Allows users to search through options. Useful when there are many choices.
doc.select_anatomy_menu: The floating area that displays the options (Options).
doc.select_anatomy_search: The input field for finding items among a large number of choices.
doc.select_anatomy_trigger: The area that displays the current value and expands the menu on click.
doc.select_best_practice_1: If there are more than 10 options, enable Searchable Select functionality to reduce the user's search burden.
doc.select_best_practice_2: If there are many related items, use Grouped options to organize them.
doc.select_choice_combobox_when: When there are a very large number of options and the user wants to narrow them down by free entry or search.
doc.select_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate input format based on the number of choices and screen space.
doc.select_choice_radio_when: When there are few options (5 or fewer) and you want to show all options at once.
doc.select_choice_select_when: When there are 6 or more options, or when you want to save space.
doc.select_custom_filter_desc: By default, a case-insensitive partial match search is performed, but you can also provide a custom filter function.
doc.select_desc: A dropdown menu for selecting one option from a predefined list
doc.select_design_intent: Selectes are components used to accurately select one option from a large number of choices within a limited display space. By hiding choices in the default state, they reduce screen complexity.
doc.select_guideline_1: Use when there are many options and space is insufficient for RadioGroups or SegmentedControls.
doc.select_guideline_2: If there are 5 or fewer options, consider using highly visible RadioButtons or SegmentedControls.
doc.select_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the select. Enter or Space opens the dropdown. Arrow keys navigate options. Escape closes without selection.
doc.select_long_desc: A dropdown menu for users to select one option from a predefined set.
doc.select_op_first: Focus first option with Home key
doc.select_op_last: Focus last option with End key
doc.select_op_next: Focus next option with down arrow key
doc.select_op_prev: Focus previous option with up arrow key
doc.select_scenario_country: Country Selection: For 200+ options, a select with search functionality is ideal.
doc.select_scenario_form: Profile Settings: A space-saving selection method when there are many items on the screen.
doc.select_title: A dropdown menu for selecting one option from a predefined list
doc.select_ts_desc: The Select component provides full type definitions.
doc.select_var_native_desc: Enables the browser-standard `<select>` element. In modern browsers (e.g., Chrome 119+), separators are supported within native selects using `<hr>`. Options with `type: "separator"` will be rendered as `<hr>`.
doc.select_var_sep_desc: A dividing line can be displayed between options by specifying `type: "separator"`.
doc.smartsearchinput_a11y_label: The textarea uses its label for accessibility. The clear button includes an accessible aria-label. Character count is announced via aria-live='polite'.
doc.smartsearchinput_best_practice_1: Set a clear placeholder that hints at both search and prompt use cases, for example 'Search or ask a question…'.
doc.smartsearchinput_best_practice_2: Use maxLength with character count display when the downstream API has token or character limits.
doc.smartsearchinput_choice_alt_when: When a fixed single-line search is sufficient (use SearchInput).
doc.smartsearchinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the input length and interaction model needed.
doc.smartsearchinput_choice_self_when: When the field needs to handle both short search queries and long AI prompts, or when auto-expanding behaviour is required.
doc.smartsearchinput_content_placeholder: Use a sample sentence the user might actually type (e.g., 'What types of buttons are in WIM UI?') as the placeholder.
doc.smartsearchinput_design_intent: SmartSearchInput addresses the growing need for inputs that serve dual roles: quick keyword search and long-form prompt entry. The textarea grows on demand so users never feel constrained, while Enter-to-submit and Shift+Enter-for-newline provide intuitive keyboard behaviour familiar from chat interfaces.
doc.smartsearchinput_keyboard_desc: Enter submits the current value (calls onSubmit). Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Tab moves focus out of the field.
doc.smartsearchinput_long_desc: An auto-expanding search input that seamlessly transitions into a multiline prompt area, bridging the gap between standard search fields and AI prompt interfaces.
doc.smartsearchinput_scenario_ai: AI chat interface where users type natural language queries.
doc.smartsearchinput_scenario_filter: Advanced search bar that accepts multi-keyword or boolean expressions.
doc.smartsearchinput_title: An expanding search input for search and AI prompts.
doc.switch_a11y_keyboard: The Space key can be used to toggle on/off.
doc.switch_a11y_role: Uses role="switch" to inform screen readers that this is a switch control.
doc.switch_anatomy_thumb: The circular handle that slides along the track to reflect the current state.
doc.switch_anatomy_track: The background element that visually indicates the on/off state via color change.
doc.switch_best_practice_1: Use a Switch only for settings that take effect immediately — if the change requires a form submission, use a Checkbox instead.
doc.switch_best_practice_2: Label the Switch with a noun phrase describing the feature being toggled (e.g., 'Dark mode'), not a verb phrase like 'Enable dark mode'.
doc.switch_choice_check_when: When the change takes effect only after a form submission or confirmation.
doc.switch_choice_matrix_desc: Choose the most appropriate component based on when the change takes effect.
doc.switch_choice_switch_when: When toggling a feature immediately changes the application state (e.g. dark mode, notifications).
doc.switch_desc: A binary switch for instantly toggling settings between on and off states
doc.switch_design_intent: A Switch is used when the user needs to toggle a single setting that takes effect immediately. Unlike a Checkbox, a Switch implies immediate action without requiring a submit button.
doc.switch_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the switch. Space toggles the on/off state. Disabled switches are not reachable by keyboard.
doc.switch_long_desc: Switches are used to toggle the state of a single setting on or off.
doc.switch_scenario_filtering: Filtering: Toggling specific conditions on/off (e.g. In-stock items only).
doc.switch_scenario_setting: Settings Screen: Toggling notification settings, dark mode, etc.
doc.switch_scenario_settings: Settings Screen: Toggling notification settings or privacy settings.
doc.switch_title: Instantly toggle a single setting on or off
doc.switchgroup_a11y_desc: Each switch in the group is keyboard-togglable. The group uses role='group' with an aria-label describing the collection.
doc.switchgroup_a11y_list: Groups switches together using list markup or role="group" to clarify their logical relationship to screen readers.
doc.switchgroup_anatomy_items: Individual settings consisting of a toggle switch and a descriptive label.
doc.switchgroup_anatomy_label: A title that indicates the overall category of settings.
doc.switchgroup_best_practice_1: Clearly label each switch with a descriptive label so users understand what they are toggling.
doc.switchgroup_best_practice_2: Consider grouping related toggles under a fieldset with a legend for better semantic structure.
doc.switchgroup_choice_alt_when: When a single binary toggle is needed (use Switch) or when selecting from a list (use CheckboxGroup).
doc.switchgroup_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether toggles should be grouped or independent.
doc.switchgroup_choice_self_when: When managing multiple related on/off toggles together (e.g., notification preferences).
doc.switchgroup_content_immediate: Since switches often imply immediate reflection, ensure that the UI clearly communicates that each setting has been updated.
doc.switchgroup_design_intent: SwitchGroup is a component for managing multiple related toggle switches collectively. It is suitable for control panels where users need to turn multiple optional features or types of notifications on or off.
doc.switchgroup_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus to the switch group. Space toggles individual switches. Arrow keys move between options.
doc.switchgroup_long_desc: A group of switch components used to handle multiple toggle selections.
doc.switchgroup_motion_active: When a switch is toggled, visual feedback is provided immediately through color and position changes.
doc.switchgroup_scenario_notify: Toggling different types of notifications (Email, SMS, Push).
doc.textarea_a11y_desc: When entering long sentences, clarify the focus state so that users do not lose sight of their entry position, and communicate entry limits etc. with aria-describedby as needed.
doc.textarea_anatomy_field: An editable area that accepts multiple lines of text.
doc.textarea_anatomy_resize: A part that allows users to manually adjust the height (browser function or style setting).
doc.textarea_best_practice_1: Set a reasonable default height and allow resizing so users can accommodate varying text lengths.
doc.textarea_best_practice_2: Show character count or limit when there is a maximum length to help users manage their input.
doc.textarea_choice_input_when: When entering short, single pieces of information such as names, addresses (partial), or phone numbers.
doc.textarea_choice_matrix_desc: Select according to the amount and quality of information expected to be entered.
doc.textarea_choice_textarea_when: When entry of sentences of several lines or more is anticipated (e.g., contact details).
doc.textarea_content_prefill: If the entry content is unclear, present concrete description examples as placeholders or help text.
doc.textarea_design_intent: Textarea is a component for enabling entry of long-form plain text such as descriptions, comments, or messages. It provides a wider entry area than a standard Input and increases the degree of freedom in writing by supporting scrolling and (where necessary) automatic resizing.
doc.textarea_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the textarea field. Standard keyboard input including Enter for new lines is supported. Escape cancels where applicable.
doc.textarea_scenario_comment: Entering long comments for photos or videos.
doc.textarea_scenario_contact: Sending question content in a free-form description format.
doc.textarea_title: Multi-line text field optimized for long-form input
doc.textarea_var_ghost_desc: A simple style without a background color. Does not emphasize it as an input field by default, but provides visual feedback on hover or focus.
doc.themetoggle_a11y_1: The icon variant is a single button with an aria-label that names both the action and the current mode.
doc.themetoggle_a11y_2: The segmented variant is a labelled group whose buttons expose aria-pressed to convey the active mode.
doc.themetoggle_a11y_3: Every mode carries a text label, so its meaning never depends on the icon alone.
doc.themetoggle_choice_alt_when: Build an unrelated segmented option group.
doc.themetoggle_choice_matrix_desc: Use ThemeToggle for the theme switch specifically, and a generic SegmentedControl only when you need a non-theme option group.
doc.themetoggle_choice_self_when: Switch the app theme with persistence and system fallback handled for you.
doc.themetoggle_design_intent: Dark mode is only as good as its switch. ThemeToggle turns the token system's data-theme contract into a ready-made control, so apps do not reinvent persistence, system-preference fallback, and accessible labelling every time.
doc.themetoggle_keyboard_desc: The control is a standard button (or group of buttons): Tab moves focus to it, and Enter or Space activates the focused option.
doc.themetoggle_long_desc: ThemeToggle switches the app between light, dark, and system themes. It writes data-theme to the document root — the attribute the design tokens key off — and persists the choice to localStorage.
doc.themetoggle_practice_1: Keep the system option so returning users inherit their OS preference until they choose otherwise.
doc.themetoggle_practice_2: Apply the stored theme before first paint (an inline script in the document head) to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.
doc.themetoggle_practice_3: Place the toggle in a consistent, predictable spot such as the header or settings, not scattered per page.
doc.themetoggle_scenario_1_desc: The compact icon variant sits in the top bar and cycles light and dark with one click.
doc.themetoggle_scenario_2_desc: The segmented variant offers light, dark, and system as an explicit, discoverable choice.
